claim: AWS Data Exchange contains more than 3,500 data products from domains including financial services, healthcare and life sciences, geospatial, weather, and mapping.
question: What type of data can you subscribe to on AWS Data Exchange?

evidence.quote: Today, AWS Data Exchange contains more than 3,500 data products from a broad range of domains, including financial services (for example, top US businesses by revenue); healthcare and life sciences (for example, population health management); geospatial (for example, satellite imagery); weather (for example, historical and future trajectories of temperature); and mapping (for example, street level imagery and foot traffic patterns).

claim: As a subscriber with an active subscription, you receive an Amazon CloudWatch Events event from AWS Data Exchange every time the provider publishes new revisions, which you can use to automate consumption of new data.
question: How do you know when new revisions of a subscribed data set become available?

evidence.quote: As a subscriber with an active subscription to a product, you'll receive an Amazon CloudWatch Events event from AWS Data Exchange every time the provider publishes new revisions. You can use this CloudWatch event to automate consumption of new data.

claim: AWS Data Exchange sends a CloudWatch Events event as new data is published, so you can automate ingestion without managing physical media or FTP credentials, and it stores copies of the data you have licensed so you can access point-in-time history in one secure location.

values.display: point-in-time history all in one secure location

evidence.quote: AWS Data Exchange sends you a CloudWatch Events event as new data is published, allowing you to automate ingestion without having to manage any physical media, FTP credentials, or other legacy technology. It also stores copies of data you've licensed, allowing you to access point-in-time history all in one secure location.

claim: Data in AWS Data Exchange is organized using three building blocks: data sets, revisions, and assets.
question: How is data organized in AWS Data Exchange?

evidence.quote: Data in AWS Data Exchange is organized using three building blocks: data sets, revisions, and assets.

claim: A data set is a container for data that belongs together, and data sets contain a series of revisions that data providers publish as needed to make new assets available.
question: What is a data set in AWS Data Exchange and what does it contain?

values.display: container for data that belongs together

evidence.quote: A data set is a container for data that belongs together (for example, end of data pricing for equities trading in the US). Data sets contain a series of revisions, which data providers publish as needed to make new assets available.

claim: Assets are any file that can be stored in Amazon S3, for example CSV, Parquet, or image files.
question: What is an asset in AWS Data Exchange?

values.display: any file that can be stored in Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3)

evidence.quote: Assets are any file that can be stored in Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) (for example, CSV, Parquet, or image files).
